title: 1960 AHSME Problem 9
statement: The fraction \[ \frac{a^2+b^2-c^2+2ab}{a^2+c^2-b^2+2ac} \] is (with suitable restrictions on the values of \(a,\) \(b,\) and \(c\)):

answerChoices.label: C
answerChoices.text: reducible to a polynomial of three terms

solutions.text:
Factoring gives \[ \begin{gathered} a^2+b^2-c^2+2ab\\ {}=(a+b-c)(a+b+c),\\ a^2+c^2-b^2+2ac\\ {}=(a-b+c)(a+b+c). \end{gathered} \] Cancelling the common factor, under the stated suitable restrictions, leaves \[ \frac{a+b-c}{a-b+c}. \]

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: Rewrite each quadratic expression as a difference of squares
The numerator and denominator share a factor \(a+b+c\)
